# An agent says what it is

The agent posts in a thread where people also write, or replies to a person.

## Answer

Every agent message carries marks no person's message has: an icon avatar instead of a photo, and the agent's own name. When the product knows which model wrote the reply, it shows the model name in small text next to the time. An agent the workspace connects from outside gets a plain bot icon, not the product's logo.

## Why

People must see at a glance whether a person or an agent wrote what they are reading, and whose agent it is.

## Do

- Show the agent with an icon avatar, never a photo or an initial.
- Name the agent in the message header: its role or given name, or 'Agent' when it has none.
- Show the model name next to the time when the product knows it.
- Give an agent from outside the product a plain bot icon, not the product's logo.

## Don't

- Do not show a photo for an agent, even when one is set.
- Do not show the product's logo on an agent the product does not run.

## Native

On Apple an 'Agent' label with a sparkles icon sits next to a named agent's name, and the app draws the agent's avatar itself.

Seen in: Scindo.
